div.head: II Cn 57
div.ab: Gif hwa ymb cininge oððe hlaford syrwe, si he his feores scyldig ⁊ ealles þæs ðe he age, butan he ga to þryfealdan ordale.
Lafordes syrwunge. Gyf hwa embe kinincg syrwe oððe ymbe his hlaford, sy he his feores scyldig ⁊ ealles ðæs ðe he age, buton he ga to ðryfealdan ordale [⁊ þær clæne wyrþ].
Gif hwa emb cyning oððe hlaforde syrwe, sy he his feores scyldig ⁊ ealles þæs þe he age, buton he ga to þrifealdan ordale.
Si quis de morte regis uel domini sui quoquo modo tractabit, uitę suę reus sit et omnium quę habebit, nisi triplici iudicio se purget.
Qui de traditione regis aut domini sui insidiatur, careat omnium bonorum suorum et reus sit mortis, nisi se purgauerit triplici iudicio.
[57] Si quis aduersus regem uel dominum arma tulerit, sit reus et uite et uniuerse substancie, nisi triplici Dei iudicio se absoluere potuerit.
Lafordes syrwunge. Gyf hwa embe kinincg syrwe oððe ymbe his hlaford, sy he his feores scyldig ⁊ ealles ðæs ðe he age, buton he ga to ðryfealdan ordale [⁊ þær clæne wyrþ].
Gif hwa ymb ciningc oððe hlaford syrwe, si he his feores scyldig and ealles þæs ðe he age, butan he ga to þryfealdan ordale.

(Herrenverrath. B) Wenn einer dem König oder dem (seinem B) Herrn verrätherisch nachstellt, sei er [des Verlustes] seines Lebens schuldig und alles dessen, was er besitzt — es sei denn, er schreite zum dreifachen Ordal (und wird dort rein B).

(Treason against a lord. B) If anyone treacherously plots against the king or the (his, B) lord, let him be liable [to the loss] of his life and of everything he possesses, unless he goes to the threefold ordeal (and is found clean there, B).

Of plotting against a lord. If anyone plots against the king or against his own lord, he shall forfeit his life and all that he possesses, unless he goes to the triple ordeal and there proves himself innocent.
If anyone plots against the king or his lord, he is to forfeit his life and all that he owns, unless he goes to the three-fold ordeal.
If anyone conspires against the king or his own lord, his life and all that he owns shall be forfeit, unless he undergoes the threefold ordeal.

note.label: wyrþ
note.seg: Written in the margin in 16th cent. in B; om. G, A, Ld.

While this clause is based on VI Ethelred 37 (= V Ethelred 30), it omits some of the phrases, and it uses also Alfred 4.2, taking from there the inclusion of plotting against a lord who is not the king. Alfred’s code is used for the next chapters (up to 60), so this agreement is not accidental.
